subject: DPA: geozone handback, snapshot sunset and backup retention (redlines)
messages:
From: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-cloud.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Thompson <paul.thompson@acme-cloud.com>, legal@acme-cloud.com
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on snapshot sunset / handback language in the DPA

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for walking through the DPA earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we do the internal redlines:

1) Snapshots/backups: we need clarity on how long historical VM/volume snapshots are retained in each region once a customer requests data handback. Our legal team is asking for an explicit timeline and the mechanism you’ll use to provide proof of deletion.

2) Handback window: if we request a geozone handback (EU-only), please confirm whether a 30-day retrieval window is acceptable or whether you require a longer extraction window for cross-border transfers.

3) Certification: do you have a standard deletion certificate for backups and snapshots? If not, can you provide an outline of what you can produce (hashes, timestamps, SANs, audit logs)?

Attaching the redline we started — we highlighted the snapshot clause (section 4.2). Paul and legal are looping in to make sure we don’t lose continuity on incident investigations.

Appreciate a short reply so we can update our internal change log.

Best,
Lisa
Director, Cloud Compliance
Acme Cloud, Inc.

Attachment: ACME_DPA_redlines_v2.docx (docx)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot sunset / handback language in the DPA

Lisa — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Marissa and Ben have been looped for legal and technical specifics. We can iterate wording after you review these tradeoffs.

1) Snapshots/backups: We propose a two-tier window: an operational snapshot retention of 90 days in-region for active recovery, plus a separate geo-synced archival snapshot (encrypted) retained for up to 12 months only if the customer opts into archival backups. By default we do not keep archived copies beyond 90 days unless explicitly contracted. For handback we can produce a manifest of snapshot IDs and a deletion timeline.

2) Handback window: For EU-only handback we can support a 30-day export window if the customer supplies an authorized export contact and a certificate of export that covers recipients. For cross-border transfers we require a separate approval step and recommend a 45-day window to allow for export controls and legal holdups.

3) Certification: We have a deletion certificate template that includes snapshot IDs, deletion timestamps, KMS key IDs, and a hash of the exported dataset where applicable. Ben will outline the security artefacts we can provide.

Next steps: Marissa will propose precise contract language for the DPA (narrowing definitions for backup vs. operational snapshot vs. archive). If that looks good, we’ll update the redline and run a final legal review.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

—
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Lead, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DataFlow_ACME_zone_map.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-cloud.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Thompson <paul.thompson@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot sunset / handback language in the DPA

Lisa / team — following Tessa’s note, I’ve drafted suggested redline text for the DPA that aims to: 1) differentiate terms ("operational snapshot", "archival snapshot"), 2) set clear default retention, and 3) add narrow legal-hold carve-outs. Key points below, please comment on whether these tradeoffs are acceptable. I’ll push formal wording once we confirm.

Proposed behavior (summary):
- Operational snapshots: retained up to 90 days by default; customer may request export within 30 days of a handback trigger. No export allowed outside the customer-designated geozone unless both parties agree in writing.
- Archival snapshots: only created if purchased; retained up to 12 months by contract; available for export with a 45-day notice period.
- Deletion certification: upon request, Redwood will provide a Deletion Certificate containing snapshot identifiers, deletion timestamps, KMS key rotation logs, and confirmation of object tombstoning from object-store logs. The certificate does not include raw hashes of live customer data unless mutually agreed and only when technically feasible for incremental snapshots.
- Legal hold: Redwood will preserve specified snapshots beyond the standard retention if presented with a valid legal hold notice from a competent authority; preservation will be limited to the scope and duration specified in the notice.

Two redline asks from our side:
1) Remove blanket language that allows indefinite archival replication (we can accept contractual archival but not default indefinite replication).
2) Replace "proof of deletion" vague phrasing with the certificate template (I’m attaching a sample).

I’ve attached a draft redline and the deletion cert template. If Acme is okay with the distinction between operational vs archival snapshots, we can capture this in a short DPA appendix rather than bloating the core clause.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Deletion_Cert_Template.pdf (pdf); ACME_DPA_redlines_v2.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-cloud.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot sunset / handback language in the DPA

Hi all — quick technical summary of what we can and cannot guarantee today, and the artefacts we can supply for the certificate: 

What we keep by default:
- Block-level operational snapshots in-region for 90 days; immutable snapshot IDs and object-store references retained in our audit logs.
- Short-term replication metadata for high-availability (only within contracted geozones).

What we provide for deletion certification:
- Snapshot IDs & object keys (list); deletion timestamps (ISO); KMS key ID and rotation history; storage-class transition logs; and object-store tombstone events.
- For exported datasets we can optionally generate an MD5/SHA256 manifest of the exported archive at export time (requires customer acceptance in writing due to potential PII hashing concerns).

Operational constraints:
- Complete cryptographic proof-of-deletion (e.g., zero-knowledge proof) is not a standard service we offer — our cert attests to deletion events in our systems and the lack of active references.
- Backups stored on third-party archival media (rare) will be catalogued and deleted per our vendor SLAs; we will include vendor deletion confirmations in the certificate where available.

Action: I’ll prepare the technical appendix describing the manifest fields and a short checklist for an export/handback operation. If Acme needs MD5/SHA256 manifests, flag that now so we can agree handling for sensitive data.

—
Ben Carter
Security Architect, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-cloud.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot sunset / handback language in the DPA

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- Acme accepts the operational vs archival snapshot distinction. We want the 90-day default for operational snapshots and will treat archival as an add-on.
- We’d like the option to request an MD5 manifest for exported archives; Acme legal is willing to sign an addendum agreeing to the data-hash handling process. Please include the manifest option in the technical appendix.
- For handback timelines we prefer 30 days for EU-only exports; we’ll accept 45 days for cross-border with the export approval step.

Could you please: 1) circulate a concise appendix we can attach to the DPA capturing the manifest fields, certificate template, and export workflow; and 2) send the updated redline (docx) with the operational/archive language swapped in? If we get those by EOD Monday we’ll fast-track legal approval.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lisa
Director, Cloud Compliance
Acme Cloud, Inc.
